native_result.query: How does the consideration of academic characteristics alter the effects of Socioeconomic Status and race on BA degree completion?
native_result.HypoA: When academic characteristics are considered, the effect of SES on BA degree completion is reduced and the effect of race is enlarged.
native_result.HypoB: Academic characteristics (ASVAB ability) mediate roughly half of the SES effect on educational attainment (BA-completion proxy): the SES gradient halves (~50% attenuation; ~54% of the effect indirect, 95% CI 45–61%) once ability is controlled, with a significant residual direct SES effect and a significant SES×ability interaction. Academic ability also accounts for essentially the entire Black attainment gap (which disappears after controlling ability, via a significant negative indirect path), while the Hispanic effect is a suppression (a positive direct effect masked by lower average ability). The race 'attenuation' is a suppression, not a clean mediation.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Audited data/nls_raw.csv (N=12,686, 61 cols): confirmed NO direct BA-degree variable; ASVAB 'Z-score' columns are raw ASVAB scores (mean~475) and were re-standardized. 2) Variables: outcome = highest-grade-completed 1979 (primary, continuous) + ever-in-college-dorm 1981-1996 (cross-validation, binary); SES = standardized mean of log family net income 1979 and max(parent education) [wealth 1985/1990/1996 as sensitivity]; race = 3-category (Black/Hispanic/non-Black-non-Hispanic ref); academic characteristics = mean of 4 standardized ASVAB sections. 3) Model A (SES + race dummies + controls: sex, age1979, family size) vs Model B (+ ASVAB) on complete cases N=7522, heteroskedasticity-robust SE (HC1 OLS / HC0 logit); reported coef/SE/p and attenuation ratio for SES and each race dummy. 4) Bootstrap (2000) causal mediation: total/direct/indirect + mediation proportion with 95% CIs (each X holding the other race groups + SES + demographics constant). 5) Interaction terms SES*ASVAB, Black*ASVAB, Hispanic*ASVAB. 6) Robustness: college-dorm outcome (logit), binary race, single-component SES (income/parent-ed/wealth/full), MICE m=20 (OLS chained equations, Rubin pooling), and Sample-ID (20 strata) fixed effects. Executed script: master_analysis.py (Parts 1-6, runs end-to-end ~1.5 min); outputs: combined_results.txt.
